# scholarshipportal.com API

Search scholarships, academic programmes, universities, and get reference data (countries, disciplines) from StudyPortals/ScholarshipPortal.

## Install / import

```python
from parse_apis.scholarshipportal_com_api import ScholarshipPortal
```

## Operations

Call these on the client's collection accessors (e.g. `client.<collection>.<op>(…)`) or via active-record navigation on returned objects — see [`example.py`](./example.py) for the exact call spelling. List operations return a lazy `Paginator`.

| Call | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `client.countries.list(study_level: Optional[StudyLevel \| Literal['phd', 'master', 'bachelor']] = None, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Country]` | Retrieve the list of available countries and their programme counts for a given study level. Useful for discovering valid country_iso values for search filters on search_scholarships and search_programmes. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.programmes.search(query: Optional[str] = None, offset: Optional[int] = None, country_iso: Optional[str] = None, study_level: Optional[StudyLevel \| Literal['phd', 'master', 'bachelor']] = None, discipline_ids: Optional[str] = None, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Programme]` | Search for academic programmes (MSc, PhD, etc.) with filters for study level, country, discipline, and keyword. Returns paginated results including university, location, tuition, and duration. Pagination is offset-based. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.disciplines.list(study_level: Optional[StudyLevel \| Literal['phd', 'master', 'bachelor']] = None, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Discipline]` | Retrieve the list of available academic disciplines and their programme counts for a given study level. Useful for discovering valid discipline_ids values for search filters on search_scholarships and search_programmes. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.universities.search(query: Optional[str] = None, offset: Optional[int] = None, study_level: Optional[StudyLevel \| Literal['phd', 'master', 'bachelor']] = None, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[University]` | Search for universities with optional keyword filter. Returns paginated results with summary, location, ranking, and programme/scholarship counts. Pagination is offset-based. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.scholarships.search(query: Optional[str] = None, offset: Optional[int] = None, country_iso: Optional[str] = None, study_level: Optional[StudyLevel \| Literal['phd', 'master', 'bachelor']] = None, discipline_ids: Optional[str] = None, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Scholarship]` | Search for scholarships with filters for study level, country, discipline, and keyword. Returns paginated results. Each scholarship includes grant details, deadline, provider info, and a URL slug for fetching full details via get_scholarship_details. Pagination is offset-based; advance by incrementing offset by limit. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `scholarship.details()` | `ScholarshipDetail` | Get detailed information for a specific scholarship by its ID and slug. Returns structured data including about text, eligibility summary, and JSON-LD metadata. The id and slug are obtained from search_scholarships results. |

## Errors

| Error | Raised when | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `ScholarshipNotFound` | The scholarship ID/slug combination does not exist (404 or 410 response) | `id`, `slug` |

Runtime errors (`RateLimitError`, `UpstreamError`, `PaginationLimitError`, …) are importable from `parse_apis` and can occur on any call.

> **Note.** Some params accept an enum whose corresponding output field is raw `str`/`list` (the wire value isn't bound to the enum). Enum members never compare equal to raw strings — compare such output values against `member.value`, or use plain string literals.
